title: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2: fused ops, ROPE/rotary fixes, KV-batching + scheduler tweaks
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token cost and tail latency for long-context generation workloads by upgrading our attention implementation to FlashAttentionV2 and applying a set of fused operator optimizations. This PR combines: 1) FlashAttentionV2 kernels with rotary/ROPE compatibility fixes for our model variants, 2) fused QKV and projection ops to reduce kernel launch overhead, 3) KV-cache-aware batching and a small scheduler change to prioritize KV-friendly coalescing, and 4) fallbacks for older CUDA/toolkit environments.

Summary of changes: consolidated implementation so runtime chooses FlashAttnV2 when device capabilities and model config permit; added fused ops for QKV+proj to reduce memory traffic and launches; implemented ROPE/rotary handling edge-case fixes (2D position encodings, interleaved dims) exposed by some LLaMA and Mistral forks; updated continuous-batching scheduler to prefer merging requests that share KV-cache shape to avoid unnecessary cache rebuilds; added a compatibility shim for cuda < 12.1 to continue using legacy kernels.

Testing and benchmarking: microbenchmarks show 18-27% throughput improvement for decoder-only 16k-context generation on A100 and H100 for batch sizes 1-8, and median p99 latency reduced by ~12% in the production canary. E2E smoke tests, unit kernel tests, and the perf benchmark suite were run. See CI checks for details.

Rollout plan: staged canary on redwood-dedicated-prod -> 10% hosted traffic -> full rollout with automatic rollback on QoS regressions (integrated with rollback hooks added in this PR).

Related: ENG-1729 (attention kernel upgrade), ENG-1794 (batching and scheduler improvements), SUP-4387 (customer-reported p99 regression on long-context generation).
